input: Source a vintage typewriter for the home study

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Vintage typewriters vary enormously — mechanical vs. electric, specific era (1920s, 1950s, 1970s), or brand (Remington, Olympia, Hermes, Underwood) — and the intended type narrows the search dramatically.
The user may want it purely as a decorative/display piece or as a fully functional typing machine, which changes what condition and working order are required.
Budget sets a hard ceiling on which models, sellers, and restoration levels are realistic — a restored Hermes 3000 can cost 10x a rough-condition machine.
Whether the user has already started looking (and where) determines whether the plan should begin with sourcing channels or with narrowing the shortlist.

Online marketplaces, local antique shops, specialist dealers, and auctions each have different timelines, risks, and hands-on inspection opportunities — knowing the preferred route shapes the action steps.
The user's definition of done — e.g., purchased and on the desk by a specific date — determines urgency and whether professional sourcing help is needed.
If the typewriter is a gift for someone else sharing the study, their tastes and needs must factor into every decision, including style, colour, and functionality.

gold.taskTitle: Source a vintage typewriter for home study
gold.taskDescription: Find and acquire a vintage typewriter to place in the user's home study.

questions.title: Which era or brand of typewriter are you after?
questions.description: Identify whether the user has a specific decade (e.g., 1940s–1960s), style (portable vs. desktop), or brand (Underwood, Hermes, Olympia, Remington) in mind.

questions.title: Will it be used for typing or just display?
questions.description: Determine whether the typewriter needs to be in full working order or is purely a decorative/aesthetic piece for the study.

questions.title: What is your budget for this purchase?
questions.description: Establish a clear price range (e.g., under £100, £100–£300, £300+) to filter realistic options and restoration expectations.

questions.title: Have you already started looking anywhere specific?
questions.description: Find out if the user has browsed eBay, Etsy, local antique shops, or specialist dealers, to avoid duplicating effort and build on existing leads.

questions.title: Do you prefer buying online or in person locally?
questions.description: Determine the preferred sourcing channel — online marketplaces, local shops/fairs, or specialist dealers — as each carries different risks, inspection opportunities, and timelines.

questions.title: Is there a deadline by which you need it?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a target date (e.g., for a room reveal, event, or gift) that dictates how quickly the search must move.

questions.title: Is this for yourself or as a gift for someone else?
questions.description: Clarify who the typewriter is ultimately for, as a recipient's personal tastes, favourite colours, or specific needs may heavily influence the choice.
